reviews.body:
Thanks for this, Ollama silently ignoring `--maxtokens` and `--topk` is exactly the kind of thing that makes people think the flags are broken. Mapping them to `num_predict` and `top_k`, and only when they're greater than zero, is right, and the request-body tests cover both the set and unset paths.

Two things:

1. **This overlaps #1903**, which you opened a few hours earlier for the `num_predict` half. Both edit the same lines of `ollama.go` and both add `mockIAIConfig` to `ollama_test.go`, so they can't both merge. This one is the superset, so I'd suggest keeping it and closing #1903. I've flagged that for the maintainer.
2. **The description says nothing changes when the flags are unset, but `auth add` stores `maxtokens: 2048` and `topk: 50` by default** (`cmd/auth/add.go` lines 181 and 183). So most existing Ollama providers will now be capped at 2048 output tokens and use top-k 50. That's probably what users expected all along, but please say so in the description so the release notes don't surprise anyone.

Also, the `validate` check fails only on the title scope (this repo allows `deps` only): `fix: send --maxtokens and --topk to Ollama` will pass. Build and tests are green at `429dc00`.

Thanks for adding the behaviour note, that's exactly what the release notes need. Delta checked: `23bddec` has the same tree as `429dc00`, only the commit message changed, and `validate`, build and tests are green.

The 2048-token cap for providers created with `auth add` is now written down, and it matches how the OpenAI-compatible backends already treat the stored value since #1870. Good to merge.
